algorithms.name: Amplified One-round Best-arm (repeat O(log 1/delta) times + majority vote)

conditions: a serial algorithm with guarantee c_A sum 1/(Delta_i^eps)^2 log(|A|/Delta_i^eps) is available

source.label: thm:oneround
source.quote: Algorithm \ref{alg:oneround} identifies the best arm correctly with probability at least $2/3$ using no more than $\OO{\frac{1}{\sqrt{k}} \cdot \sum_{i=2}^{n} \frac{1}{\Del_i^2} \log \frac{n}{\Del_i}}$ arm pulls per player, provided that $6 \le \sqrt{k} \le n$. The algorithm uses a single communication round, in which each player communicates $\tO(1)$ bits.

results.notes: Pulls per player. Paper's n = K arms, k = N players.

conditions: implicitly 6 <= sqrt(k) <= n as in Theorem 3.1

source.quote: There exists a $k$-player algorithm that given $\OO{\frac{1}{\sqrt{k}} \cdot \sum_{i=2}^{n} \frac{1}{\Del_i^2} \log \frac{n}{\Del_i} \log \frac{1}{\del}}$ arm pulls, identifies the best arm correctly with probability at least $1-\del$. The algorithm uses a single communication round, in which each player communicates $O(\log(1/\delta))$ numerical values.

results.notes: Pulls per player (implicit). Condition on k inherited from Theorem 3.1 not restated.

source.label: thm:oneround_eps
source.quote: Algorithm \ref{alg:oneround_eps} identifies a $2\eps$-best arm with probability at least $2/3$ using no more than $\OO{\frac{1}{\sqrt{k}} \cdot \sum_{i=2}^{n} \frac{1}{(\Del_i^\eps)^2} \log \frac{n}{\Del_i^\eps}}$ arm pulls per player, provided that $24 \le \sqrt{k} \le n$.

results.notes: Sum is over i=2..n (all arms except the best), which sum_subopt approximates. Delta_i^eps = max(Delta_i, eps).

source.label: thm:main1
source.quote: With probability at least $1-\del$, Algorithm \ref{alg:algname} identifies the optimal arm using $\OO{\frac{1}{k} \cdot \sum_{i=2}^{n} \frac{1}{(\Dele_i)^2} \log \left(\frac{n}{\del} \log \frac{1}{\Dele_i}\right)}$ arm pulls per~player; terminates after no more than $1+\ceil{\log_2(1/\eps)}$ rounds of communication (or after $1+\ceil{\log_2(1/\Del_\st)}$ rounds for $\eps=0$).

results.notes: Uses 1+ceil(log2(1/eps)) communication rounds. Theorem says 'optimal arm' but proof shows eps-optimal arm.

source.label: cor:main3
source.quote: Given a parameter $R > 0$, set $\eps_r \gets \eps^{r/R}$ for all $r \ge 1$ in Algorithm \ref{alg:algname}. With~probability at least $1-\del$, the modified algorithm identifies an $\eps$-best arm using $\tO\lr{\frac{\eps^{-2/R}}{k} \cdot \sum_{i=2}^{n} \frac{1}{(\Dele_i)^2}}$ arm pulls per player; terminates after at most $R$ rounds of communication.

symbols.T_ser: integer T such that a single-player algorithm identifies the best arm w.p. 2/3 with O_tilde(T) pulls on the same instance

conditions: exists an instance (rewards a random permutation of 1/2+Delta, 1/2-Delta, 0,...,0 with Delta = 1/sqrt(n))
single communication round at end of game

source.label: thm:lb1
source.quote: There exist rewards $p_1,\ldots,p_n \in [0,1]$ and integer $T$ such that for any $k$-player strategy that uses a single round of communication at the end of the game, each individual player must use at least $T/\sqrt{k}$ arm pulls for them to collectively identify the best arm with probability at least $2/3$; there exist a single-player algorithm that needs at most $\tO(T)$ pulls for identifying the best arm with probability at least $2/3$.

results.notes: Existential instance lower bound showing sqrt(k) speed-up is optimal up to logs; per-player pull count. Proof uses T ~ c1*n.
